prompt:
Create a finished illustration for a public book-summary library for adult readers. Use a calm, contemporary illustrated-book style: hand-painted gouache, soft matte pigment, restrained pencil details, and a subtle warm ivory paper texture. Use a consistent palette of muted sage and olive green, warm ochre, natural wood brown, and warm ivory, with dark brown or charcoal details. Keep saturation restrained and lighting soft and natural. Give the scene generous breathing room, a clear focal point, and simple, recognizable forms that remain readable on a phone. When people are relevant, depict believable adults with natural proportions, respectful expressions, and ordinary clothing. Use the same medium, palette, texture, and level of detail across the illustration. Avoid photorealism, glossy 3D, neon colors, cinematic effects, heavy black outlines, childish clipart, ornamental clutter, and a different art style in each panel. No readable text, captions, logos, watermarks, fake book covers, or invented author portraits. Keep all explanations and essential labels outside the generated image.

Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: finished SQUARE hero illustration for a
book-summary article. The supplied reference is a STYLE REFERENCE ONLY. Match its
gouache, paper texture, matte pigments and gentle natural light. Do not copy its
person, study desk, notebook or scene. Use a NEW concrete subject and composition
appropriate to the book below. Choose a clear single scene or visual metaphor that
conveys the central idea, using the summary as context. Do not render the title,
author name, quotations, text, labels, equations or a book cover. No random abstract
shards, generic tech networks, diagram labels, glossy objects or flat-vector icons.
Avoid a person at a study desk as a default. Use people only when they help explain
this particular subject. For biographies, evoke the person's work, historical
setting or defining subject through places and objects, without inventing an author
or historical person's likeness. Do not depict a speculative documentary event.
For novels, choose an appropriate setting, object or restrained symbolic scene;
preserve the work's tone without graphic violence, sexual imagery or fake covers.
For scientific or medical topics, favor truthful everyday or natural objects and
avoid inventing scientific diagrams, anatomy, measurements or therapeutic results.
Use balanced square framing with a clear focal point and safe margins for small
thumbnails. Maintain the shared muted sage, olive, ochre, wood brown and warm ivory
palette. Make the illustration clearly hand-painted rather than photographic.

{"title": "How Music Works by David Byrne", "description": "David Byrne explains how rooms, recording technology, collaboration, money, and communities shape the music we make and hear.", "excerpt": "\n\n## Music Takes the Shape of Its Surroundings\n\nA song can feel intimate through headphones, lose its detail in a reverberant hall, or become a shared physical experience on a dance floor. In *How Music Works*, David Byrne asks us to take those differences seriously. The surroundings of music help determine its form, its meaning, and whether anyone gets to hear it.\n\nDrawing on Talking Heads and his collaborations, Byrne combines a musician's working experience with reflections on architecture, technology, economics, and cultural participation. His career supplies examples rather than a continuous autobiography. The organizing question is how all the circumstances around a piece of music enter into the music itself. The book first appeared in 2012; the 2017 edition adds a chapter on digital curation. The [publisher's description](https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/535976/how-music-works-by-david-byrne/) identifies that expanded scope.\n\n### Creation in Reverse: The Setting Comes First\n\nByrne challenges the familiar story in which an artist experiences a powerful emotion, creates a work, and then finds somewhere to present it. Frequently, he argues, an available format comes first. Musicians absorb its possibilities and restrictions, often unconsciously, and make something that fits. Passion still matters, but it takes shape within those conditions.\n\nHis account of CBGB makes the argument concrete. The small club's clutter and irregular surfaces absorbed sound and broke up reflections. Musical details remained audible, and audiences could see intimate gestures. Such a room rewarded different choices from a vast echoing space. In a stone cathedral, lingering notes can enrich sustained singing while blurring rapid rhythmic detail. Byrne treats these contrasts as examples of music adapting to an acoustic niche. His [opening-chapter excerpt](https://www.mcsweeneys.net/articles/a-mcsweeneys-books-preview-of-david-byrnes-how-music-works) lays out this reversal.\n\nA useful implication is that constraints deserve attention before they become problems. For a performer, arranging for a room can be part of composing. For a listener, asking where music was meant to function may reveal qualities that a recording alone makes difficult to appreciate.\n\n### Recording Technol"}

Composition variety: do not reuse the reference woman's likeness, dark hair bun, study-room arrangement, mug and trailing houseplant. Do not default to a person thinking over a notebook or laptop. Choose a concrete situation appropriate to this specific book. If people are useful, the main adult should be a middle-aged man with short straight graying hair. Other people can vary naturally. Keep the same painted medium and palette. Avoid floating icons and thought bubbles; communicate through the scene itself.

## Generation prompt

Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: finished square editorial hero illustration for a thoughtful summary of David Byrne's How Music Works. Primary request: show how musical sound is shaped by its environment and recording tools. Scene: a cohesive architectural cutaway with three connected musical spaces, a lofty stone vaulted hall with a small choir, an intimate low-ceiling club with a drummer, guitarist and standing listeners, and a modest recording room with a reel-to-reel recorder, mixing desk and headphones. Flowing abstract ribbons of sound visually change from long sustained curves in the hall to short rhythmic marks in the club and layered loops in the studio. Style: refined hand-painted gouache editorial illustration, tactile paper, clear spatial storytelling, warm muted colors, detailed but calm. Composition: square at least 1024 by 1024, balanced with recognizable people and instruments, readable at article size. Constraints: no text, no labels, no lettering, no logos, no book cover, no portrait of the author, no watermark. This is a conceptual illustration rather than a historical reconstruction.

## Review

Visually inspected the saved bundle image. All three musical settings are recognizable, with sound ribbons connecting them. The illustration contains no labels, cover imitation, or author portrait. Verified the file is a real PNG exceeding 512 pixels in each dimension.
